text: Into which two main categories are ICMP messages divided based on their functions?
info: ICMP has 2 primary categories: Error-Reporting (reports issues) and Query (requests information).

text: What is the main function of Error-Reporting Messages in ICMP?
info: Error-Reporting = Sends issue notifications back to the Source Host only.

answers.text: To correct invalid data in the IP Header
To report problems encountered during IP Datagram transit back to the original source host
To query IP Address and Subnet Mask values from a Router
To compress the data packet size

text: Which of the following is classified as an ICMP Query Message?
info: Echo Request/Reply (used in Ping) and Mask Request/Reply are Query Messages.

text: Upon which protocol in the Network Layer does ICMP rely for encapsulation?
info: ICMP messages are encapsulated directly inside IP datagrams.

text: Why is ICMP not classified as a Transport Layer protocol, even though it is a software module that processes data?
info: ICMP supports IP operations at the Network Layer, so it is not considered a Transport Layer protocol.

answers.text: Because it does not directly provide data transmission services to applications, but rather assists IP
Because it transmits data at excessively high speeds
Because it uses standard TCP communication ports
Because it communicates directly with MAC Addresses

text: What is the primary difference between an Error-Reporting Message and a Query Message?
info: Error = Reports a problem / Query = Sent to request and receive specific information.

answers.text: Error-Reporting uses UDP, whereas Query uses TCP
Error-Reporting is generated when an error occurs, whereas Query is generated to request information
Error-Reporting is sent only to Routers, whereas Query is sent only to Hosts
Error-Reporting does not require a Checksum, whereas Query does

text: When an IP packet encounters an issue and an ICMP Error Report must be generated, who creates and sends this message?
info: The router or host that detects the error creates the ICMP Error message and sends it back to the source.

answers.text: The destination host or the router that encountered the problem
The source host generates it locally

text: Which of the following messages does NOT belong to the ICMP Query Message group?
info: Source Quench is an Error-Reporting Message (congestion control), not a Query.

text: ICMP Query Messages are typically sent in pairs in what manner?
info: Query messages always work in pairs: Request/Solicit and Reply/Advertise.

answers.text: Request and Reply (or Solicitation and Advertisement)

text: Which statement correctly describes the operational nature of ICMP?
info: ICMP only reports problems—it does not repair data or retransmit lost packets.

answers.text: It is a reliable protocol that guarantees packet delivery
It is a protocol that supports IP; it does not fix issues itself, but merely reports results
It replaces the IP protocol whenever an error occurs
It operates using a connection-oriented model

text: What are the first three standard fields present in every ICMP Header type?
info: The first 4 Bytes of an ICMP Header must always contain Type (1B), Code (1B), and Checksum (2B).

answers.text: Source IP, Destination IP, and TTL

text: What is the size of the Type field in the ICMP Header?
info: Type field size is 8 bits (1 Byte), representing the main message type.

text: What is the purpose of the Code field in the ICMP Header?
info: Code = Specifies the subtype/reason (e.g., Type 3 Code 3 = Port Unreachable).

answers.text: To provide additional subtype details or specific reasons for a given ICMP Type

text: Which field in the ICMP Header is used to detect packet corruption?
info: Checksum = Detects corrupted bits in transit.

text: What is the fixed size of a standard ICMP Header?
info: Standard ICMP Header is always 8 Bytes long.

text: What information is included in the Data section of an ICMP Error-Reporting packet?
info: ICMP Error attaches the original IP Header + first 8 Bytes of the failed packet payload so the source can identify the failed process.

answers.text: Original IP Header + first 8 Bytes of original IP Datagram payload
MAC Addresses of all routers on the network

text: Why must ICMP Error messages include the first 8 Bytes of the original IP Datagram payload?
info: The first 8 Bytes contain TCP/UDP source/destination port numbers, allowing the source OS to notify the specific process.

answers.text: To determine which higher-layer protocol generated the original packet (e.g., TCP/UDP Port numbers)
To enable routers to correct corrupted data

text: How many bits are allocated to each of the Identifier and Sequence Number fields in Query Messages?
info: Identifier = 16 bits, Sequence Number = 16 bits (totaling 32 bits / 4 Bytes).

text: If Type = 8 and Code = 0, which message does this packet represent?
info: Type 8, Code 0 = Echo Request (Ping outgoing packet).

text: If Type = 0 and Code = 0, which message does this packet represent?
info: Type 0, Code 0 = Echo Reply (Ping incoming response).

text: When a delivery error occurs, to which device is the ICMP Error-Reporting Message sent?
info: Error Reports are directed to the Original Source Host to notify it of the failure.

answers.text: Sent back to the original source host that created the packet
Broadcasted to all devices on the local network

text: Which Type value corresponds to the ICMP Destination Unreachable message?
info: Destination Unreachable = Type 3.

text: If the destination host receives an IP Datagram but has no matching process or port available (Unreachable Port), which ICMP Type and Code will be returned?
info: Port Unreachable = Type 3, Code 3 (used by Traceroute to verify destination arrival).

text: Under what circumstance is an ICMP Time Exceeded (Type 11) message generated?
info: Time Exceeded (Type 11) occurs when TTL reaches 0 (packet expires in transit).

answers.text: The destination host processes data too slowly
The TTL (Time to Live) field in the IP Header decrements to 0 during transit
The requested port number is not found on the destination host

text: During Reassembly (combining fragments), if the first fragment arrives but other fragments fail to arrive within the timeout period, which message is created?
info: Reassembly timer expiration = Time Exceeded (Type 11, Code 1).

text: When is an ICMP Parameter Problem (Type 12) message sent?
info: Parameter Problem (Type 12) = IP Header contains invalid/unprocessable header fields.

answers.text: When there is an error or ambiguity in header fields of the IP Datagram
When a physical LAN cable is disconnected
When data is sent faster than the receiver can handle
When the destination host is powered off

text: What is the primary objective of the ICMP Source Quench (Type 4) message?
info: Source Quench = Requests source to throttle transmission during network congestion.

answers.text: To report a broken network path
To perform flow control by asking the source host to slow down packet transmission
To request a routing path change
To test connectivity with the default gateway

text: Which device creates an ICMP Redirect (Type 5) message, and for what purpose?
info: Redirect (Type 5) = Router advises Host of a more optimal local gateway route.

answers.text: Created by a Host to change its IP Address
Created by a Router to inform a Host to use a better alternative router for a specific destination
Created by a Switch to change MAC Addresses
Created by a Server to update a URL

text: Which of the following conditions waives the generation of an ICMP Error-Reporting Message?
info: ICMP Error messages are never generated in response to ICMP Errors, Broadcast/Multicast packets, or special IP addresses.

answers.text: The original failed packet is already an ICMP Error-Reporting Message
The original packet was sent as Multicast or Broadcast
The IP Datagram has a Source Address of 0.0.0.0 or 127.0.0.1

text: What does the rule prohibiting ICMP Errors from responding to ICMP Errors aim to prevent?
info: Suppressing recursive error reports prevents endless packet looping that could crash the network.

answers.text: Infinite packet loops and broadcast storms

text: ICMP Echo Request and Echo Reply messages are utilized by which utility program?
info: Ping uses Echo Request (Type 8) and Echo Reply (Type 0).

text: If a host needs to request a Subnet Mask from a LAN Router, which pair of ICMP messages is used?
info: Address-Mask Request/Reply = Obtains Subnet Mask (Types 17 & 18).

text: In an Address-Mask Request packet (Type 17), what value is placed in the Address Mask field?
info: Request fills the mask field with 32 zeros; the router returns the real mask in Reply (Type 18).

answers.text: The actual Subnet Mask of the network
The IP Address of the Router

text: Who sends a Router Solicitation (Type 10) message, and for what purpose?
info: Solicitation = Host queries local routers to discover default gateways.

answers.text: Sent by a Router to announce its IP Address
Sent by a Host to discover IP Addresses of Routers on the network
Sent by a Host to test internet bandwidth
Sent by a Router to request Subnet Masks from Hosts

text: In a Router Advertisement packet (Type 9), what is the function of the Address preference level field?
info: Preference level determines priority order when selecting default routers.

answers.text: Ranks router desirability for selection as a Default Router
Indicates total router count in system

text: If the Address preference level field in a Router Advertisement is set to 80000000 (hexadecimal), what does this mean?
info: Preference = 0 is default candidate; Preference = 80000000 (hex) explicitly forbids selection.

answers.text: This Router is the primary Default Router
This Router MUST NOT be selected as a Default Router under any circumstances
This Router has maximum speed in network

text: Which Transport Layer protocol packet does Traceroute send, and which ICMP response is returned upon reaching the destination successfully?
info: Traceroute sends UDP to an unused port -> Target host returns Port Unreachable (Type 3, Code 3).

answers.text: Uses TCP / Responds with Echo Reply (Type 0)
Uses UDP / Responds with Destination Unreachable (Type 3, Code 3)
Uses ICMP / Responds with Time Exceeded (Type 11)
Uses UDP / Responds with Router Advertisement (Type 9)

text: How does Traceroute discover intermediate router IP Addresses (Hops)?
info: Traceroute increments TTL by 1 starting at 1 -> Intermediate routers drop packet at TTL=0 and reply with Time Exceeded (Type 11).

answers.text: Forces TTL to expire at each hop to trigger ICMP Time Exceeded (Type 11) responses
Receives ICMP Echo Replies sequentially from each router
Sends Router Advertisement queries to every router

text: If Ping sends a payload of 56 Bytes, what will be the resulting sizes of the ICMP Packet and Total IP Packet?
info: ICMP Packet = 56 (Data) + 8 (ICMP Header) = 64 Bytes. Total IP Packet = 64 + 20 (IP Header) = 84 Bytes.

answers.text: ICMP Packet = 56 bytes, Total IP Packet = 76 bytes
ICMP Packet = 64 bytes, Total IP Packet = 84 bytes
ICMP Packet = 64 bytes, Total IP Packet = 96 bytes
ICMP Packet = 84 bytes, Total IP Packet = 104 bytes

text: What components make up a 38-Byte UDP packet in Traceroute Example 4?
info: 38 Bytes = IP Header (20) + UDP Header (8) + Payload Data (10).

text: What data scope is included in the ICMP Checksum calculation?
info: ICMP Checksum covers both Header and Data (unlike IP Checksum which covers only IP Header).

answers.text: Both ICMP Header and ICMP Data
Combined IP Header and ICMP Header

text: What must be done to the Checksum field prior to calculating Checksum at the sender?
info: The Checksum field must be initialized to 0 before summing 16-bit words.

answers.text: Populate with ASCII value of message first

text: Into what size word units is an ICMP packet divided for Checksum calculation?
info: Checksum calculations group data into 16-bit (2-byte) words.

text: What mathematical method is used to compute the Checksum value?
info: Sum 16-bit words using One's complement, then invert all bits (0 -> 1, 1 -> 0).

answers.text: One's complement sum followed by bitwise complement (inversion)

text: During Checksum testing at the receiver, when is a packet considered intact and accepted?
info: Receiver validation: Summing all 16-bit words (including Checksum) and taking One's complement must yield 0000000000000000.

answers.text: Sum of 16-bit words and bitwise complement yields all 1s
Sum of 16-bit words and bitwise complement yields sixteen zeros (16 0s)
Yields value equal to Source IP Address
Yields value matching Sequence Number field

text: If the receiver's Checksum calculation does NOT result in sixteen zeros, how does the system handle the packet?
info: Checksum failure = Discard/Reject packet immediately.

answers.text: Accepts packet but logs an entry

text: When calculating Checksum for string TEST, how are letter pairs 'T' and 'E' converted into bit values?
info: Characters convert to 8-bit ASCII codes; pairing two characters forms one 16-bit word.

answers.text: 8-bit ASCII codes of each character concatenated into a 16-bit word

text: If an ICMP packet has an odd total byte count, how is it handled before Checksum calculation?
info: Odd byte length requires appending an 8-bit zero pad byte to form complete 16-bit blocks.

answers.text: Append a 0-byte (8 zero bits padding) at the end to make length even

text: Which statement is most accurate regarding Checksum in ICMP?
info: ICMP Checksum covers Header + Data; corrupted packets are silently dropped without generating error reports.

answers.text: Calculates ICMP Header only to save processing time
Calculates both ICMP Header and ICMP Data to ensure total packet integrity
Receiver skips calculation and trusts received value
If Checksum fails, ICMP immediately returns an error report to sender

text: Can Checksum correct corrupted data encountered during transit?
info: Checksum is strictly for Error Detection, not Error Correction.

answers.text: Cannot correct data; performs Error Detection only
Corrects data only if message is Query Type

text: What does ICMP Package refer to in software architecture?
info: ICMP Package = Software architecture modules managing incoming (Input) and outgoing (Output) ICMP processing.

answers.text: A pre-packaged cable set for transmitting ICMP frames
A set of software modules (Input Module and Output Module) managing ICMP packet receipt and transmission
A utility program for copying files over ICMP
A large payload field in IP Header

text: In the ICMP Package structure, when the Input Module receives a Request or Solicitation message, what action does it take?
info: Input Module handles incoming Request/Solicitation by constructing and sending Reply/Advertisement via IP Layer.

answers.text: Forwards it to TCP protocol for processing
Generates a Reply or Advertisement and immediately sends it out via IP Layer
Returns an Error Message to source
Holds data in buffer awaiting admin approval

text: If the Input Module receives an ICMP Error Message, where does it pass the information?
info: Incoming Error Message = Dispatch upward to higher-layer protocols (e.g., TCP/UDP/App).

text: What is the primary role of the Output Module in the ICMP Package?
info: Output Module constructs outgoing ICMP messages based on requests from Upper Layers or IP Layer.

answers.text: Creates Request, Solicitation, or Error Messages requested by Upper Layers or IP Layer
Translates IP Addresses to MAC Addresses

text: From which sources can the Output Module receive requests to construct ICMP messages?
info: Output Module receives requests from above (TCP/UDP/Apps) and below (IP Layer).

answers.text: Both Upper Layers and IP Layer
Cannot receive external requests; generates autonomously

text: To which layer are packets constructed by the Output Module delivered for transmission?
info: Once constructed by the Output Module, ICMP packets are sent down to the IP Layer.

text: If an application (such as Ping) needs to send a Query message, to which module does it send its request?
info: Applications invoke the Output Module to format and transmit outgoing messages.

answers.text: Directly to IP Layer bypassing ICMP Package

text: Where is the ICMP Package positioned within the software architectural stack?
info: ICMP Package sits between the lower IP Layer and higher Upper Layers.

answers.text: Between IP Layer and Upper Layers (TCP/UDP/Applications)
Between Physical Layer and Data Link Layer
Between Transport Layer and Application Layer

text: When a host receives an ICMP Echo Reply message resulting from a Ping, which module receives it and returns the result to the Ping application?
info: Inbound packet = Input Module receives packet and forwards data up to Ping application.

text: Which statement best summarizes the operation of the ICMP Package?
info: ICMP Package is situated between IP Layer and Upper Layers to handle inbound and outbound ICMP messages.

answers.text: Component of Transport Layer replacing TCP
Situated between IP Layer and Upper Layers to handle inbound and outbound ICMP messages
Translates IP Addresses to MAC Addresses
Assigns random IP Addresses to Hosts
